We need to determine crimes based on facts. The scenario: Defendant Pu (蒲某) got into a fight with Li (李某2) and assaulted her (punches, kicks). Then police arrived. Pu assaulted police: insult, kicked police's leg, punched eye, punched chest, etc. Police forced him to police station. Injuries to police: minor injuries (light injuries). So crimes: assault (故意伤害) of a private person (Li) and assault of police (妨害公务) maybe also "故意伤害" of police (since injuries). Also "侮辱" maybe? The examples: In earlier similar case (the one with dangerous driving and assaulting police) they gave "危险驾驶;妨害公务". For assault on police, the crime is "妨害公务" (obstructing public officials). Also assault causing injuries to police could be "故意伤害罪" (intentional injury). But typical Chinese law: assault on police while performing duty is "妨害公务罪" (Article 277). If causing injury, may also be "故意伤害罪" but usually counted as "妨害公务罪" with aggravating factor. In examples, they used "妨害公务" for assault on police. So we need to list crimes: "故意伤害" (for assault on Li) and "妨害公务" (for assault on police). Also maybe "聚众扰乱公共场所秩序"? No. So answer: [罪名]故意伤害;妨害公务<eoa>
